changed: Slides 1 and 2 now show positions (2026-10-08): a rook behind its passed pawn, and an active rook on the 7th against a passive one.

Punjabi: “yours or theirs” and “behind theirs it chases” now name the opponent and the rook; “worth a pawn” was ਬਰਾਬਰ (close to the draw word), now ਇੱਕ ਪਿਆਦੇ ਜਿੰਨਾ ਕੀਮਤੀ; title adds ਨਿਯਮ; practice and challenge tell the child what to do.

Punjabi, a wrong lesson in the answer: “Rd1+, pushing the king further away” and “the king must go further from the pawn” read as your own king, the opposite of the Lucena (your king stays by the pawn; the opponent’s is driven off). Both now say ਵਿਰੋਧੀ ਦੇ ਬਾਦਸ਼ਾਹ.
Punjabi: a grammar slip in slide 1 (ਤੁਹਾਡੇ ਹਾਥੀ ਨੇ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਬਾਦਸ਼ਾਹ ਨੂੰ ਕੱਟ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਹੈ); “give up the rook for it” now says for the pawn; the hint has its verbs.
Slide 2 now shows a position (2026-10-08): the pawn on your 3rd rank, the rook swinging to the far end.
Punjabi: “the king loses its hiding place” now names the opponent’s king; ਸ਼ਹਿ ਖਾਧੇ ਬਿਨਾਂ → ਸ਼ਹਿ ਮਿਲੇ ਬਿਨਾਂ; “too late now” reads correctly; the draw drills now all say ਬਰਾਬਰੀ ਬਚਾਓ.
ask: Not changed: ranks are written ਲੇਟਵੀਂ ਕਤਾਰ (“horizontal row”) through Level 9. A bare ਕਤਾਰ also means a rank, but in a level full of files the explicit word is clearer, so I kept it. Say if you want it shortened.

changed: Slides 1 and 2 now show positions (2026-10-08): Black in zugzwang, and a waiting pawn move that hands the move back.
Punjabi: ਕਦੇ (“ever”) → ਕਦੇ-ਕਦੇ (“sometimes”); practice and challenge tell the child what to do.
Slide 1 now shows a position (2026-10-08): pawns on both wings.
Punjabi: “both wings” is now ਬਿਸਾਤ ਦੇ ਦੋਵੇਂ ਪਾਸੇ; the wrong bishop “can’t reach” the corner; the Try says ਬਰਾਬਰੀ ਬਚਾਓ; practice and challenge tell the child what to do.
Slides 1 and 2 now show positions (2026-10-08): a king sheltering behind its pawn, and an endless check (Qh5+ Kg8 Qe8+ Kh7, every king move forced).
Punjabi, slide 2: “a draw by repetition” now reads as a sentence; practice and challenge tell the child what to do.
Slides 1 and 2 now show positions (2026-10-08): trading rooks a pawn up, and the king coming first.
Punjabi: “they are what will queen” said ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ, the same word the lesson uses for the opponent; now ਪਿਆਦਿਆਂ. “Their counterplay” and “they offer” name the opponent; “fight back” is ਟੱਕਰ ਦੇਣ.
Slide 2 now shows a position (2026-10-08): the black king has run to the a-pawn; White’s king goes for g6.

Punjabi: “the a-file” was a bare ਕਤਾਰ (a rank); now a ਖੜ੍ਹੀ ਕਤਾਰ. “Yours wins the kingside” had become “your king-side wins”; now ਤੁਹਾਡਾ ਬਾਦਸ਼ਾਹ ਬਾਦਸ਼ਾਹ ਵਾਲੇ ਪਾਸੇ ਦੇ ਪਿਆਦੇ ਜਿੱਤ ਲੈਂਦਾ ਹੈ. Every “the king” now says whose.

Chess, the whole lesson’s position: Black’s “extra” pawn on b4 simply hung: Stockfish’s first move was Bxb4, so White was never really a pawn down. The challenge had the same flaw. Black’s pawn is now on b3, guarded by Black’s light bishop, which White’s dark bishop can never attack. Now White truly is a pawn down and holds exactly as the slide says, by guarding b2 (both hold at 0.00; in the challenge Kd4 and Bb4 lose). Slide 2 now marks b2 and the bishop’s route to c3.

Hint, both languages: Keep your bishop guarding b2, the square the b-pawn must cross, and your king close to your own f-pawn. (The old one said “in front of the f-pawn”, but that pawn was blocked already; the danger is Black’s king winning White’s f4.)
Punjabi: “fight yours” had become “fight with you”; now ਤੁਹਾਡੇ ਊਠ ਨਾਲ. One term, ਉਲਟ ਰੰਗਾਂ ਦੇ ਊਠ, throughout.
